## Does adding hierarchy move the population curve?

The point of the lineage is not abstract model fit but whether the added structure *changes what the model says about a typical child*. It does — but selectively. Hierarchy leaves the **comprehension** trajectory broadly in place while markedly relocating early **production**. @tbl-lineage-curve reads the fitted posteriors at the two ages where the steps differ most.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-lineage-curve
#| tbl-cap: "Effect of each lineage step on the typical-child trajectory, read from the fitted posteriors (medians). Words understood and spoken are expected counts out of the 800-item reference inventory; $q$ is the production ratio $P(\\text{speak}\\mid\\text{understood})$. Comprehension is broadly stable across the lineage; the early production ratio falls roughly five-fold, almost entirely at the VG08 → VG09 step that adds subject random intercepts on $q$."
#| echo: false
import pandas as pd

_steps = [
    ("VG05", "VG05 — joint baseline"),
    ("VG07", "VG07 — + study RE"),
    ("VG08", "VG08 — + subject RE on $U$"),
    ("VG09", "VG09 — + subject RE on $q$"),
    ("VG10", "VG10 — + anchored (record)"),
]


def _q(model_id, age):
    v = val(model_id, "posterior_summary_q", age, "q_median")
    return None if v is None else round(float(v), 2)


_rows = [
    {
        "Step": label,
        "Understood, 24 mo": words(model_id, "posterior_summary_u", 24),
        "Spoken, 24 mo": words(model_id, "posterior_summary_s", 24),
        "q, 24 mo": _q(model_id, 24),
        "q, 48 mo": _q(model_id, 48),
    }
    for model_id, label in _steps
]

_have_fits = val("VG10", "posterior_summary_q", 24, "q_median") is not None
show_or_pending(pd.DataFrame(_rows) if _have_fits else None, "the lineage curve-shift comparison")
```

**Comprehension is regularised, not relocated.** Words understood at 24 months stays within a narrow band across all five specifications (@tbl-lineage-curve). Adding study and subject random intercepts (@sec-randomeffects) widens the receptive curve's credible intervals to reflect between-study and between-child variation, but it does not move the receptive level.

**Early production is relocated, at one decisive step.** The typical-child production ratio $q$ at 24 months falls from about `{python} f'{val("VG05","posterior_summary_q",24,"q_median"):.2f}'` in the joint baseline (VG05) to about `{python} f'{val("VG10","posterior_summary_q",24,"q_median"):.2f}'` in the model of record (VG10) — a roughly five-fold reduction. It is not gradual: study random intercepts (VG07) and subject intercepts on *comprehension* (VG08) barely move it (≈ `{python} f'{val("VG08","posterior_summary_q",24,"q_median"):.2f}'`). The decisive change is **placing subject random intercepts on the production ratio itself** (VG08 → VG09), which alone takes $q$ at 24 months from ≈ `{python} f'{val("VG08","posterior_summary_q",24,"q_median"):.2f}'` to ≈ `{python} f'{val("VG09","posterior_summary_q",24,"q_median"):.2f}'`; the VG10 anchoring (@sec-gpanchor) then settles it at ≈ `{python} f'{val("VG10","posterior_summary_q",24,"q_median"):.2f}'`. Early spoken-word counts move with it — from about `{python} words("VG05","posterior_summary_s",24)` words at 24 months to about `{python} words("VG10","posterior_summary_s",24)`.

**The shift is genuine, and concentrated in the early years.** The mechanism is informative rather than merely technical: the pooled population average is inflated by a minority of early talkers, so once each child is allowed their own production level, the *typical* child is seen to say a much smaller fraction of understood words in the third year than the pooled mean implies. This is a real change to the headline, not cosmetic sharpening. It is also strongly age-dependent — the specifications diverge about five-fold at 24 months but reconverge by 48 months, where all of them cross $q \approx 0.5$ and the model of record nearly coincides with the baseline (VG10 `{python} f'{val("VG10","posterior_summary_q",48,"q_median"):.2f}'` vs VG05 `{python} f'{val("VG05","posterior_summary_q",48,"q_median"):.2f}'`). Hierarchy therefore changes what the model says about the early years — the period most relevant to expectations and early intervention — while leaving the mid-childhood picture essentially unchanged. This is why the findings (@sec-findings-ds) report the production ratio from VG10 rather than from any pooled specification.
